issue_context.title: Implement "Go To Last Edit Location"
issue_context.body:
### Check for existing issues

- [X] Completed

### Describe the feature

Pretty much every major IDE has it:

* VS Code: `workbench.action.navigateToLastEditLocation`
* JetBrains: Keymap -> Main Menu -> Navigate -> Last Edit Location
* Eclipse: Go to Last Edit Location

Zed, on the other hand, does not seem to have it. I'm pretty used to it and use it a lot along with history navigation, so I would appreciate if it appears in Zed.
Thanks!

### If applicable, add mockups / screenshots to help present your vision of the feature


When pressed, editor should jump to the file and caret position where the last edit was made.
comments: @skejeton, this is different, and I use it too. If you switch between different tabs and code locations without changing anything, `pane::GoBack` will walk you through them all. Last edit location is where you actually changed something for the last time.

@frozenspider, interesting. In Vim mode, moving the cursor in Normal mode and using `pane::GoBack`, does exactly what the issue describes. In insert mode (And thus probably, the VSCode keybindings) however, this is not the case.

+1 for this feature. Zed is a beautiful piece of engineering I want to use as my daily driver. I'm often working on a specific piece of code, navigate away to investigate something, then want to **immediately** go right back to where I was last **editing**.  I use a key binding for this in VSCode.  The overhead of navigating back back back.. verifying at each step if I'm where I intended to be before making further edits...seems like unnecessary cognitive burden (considering how many times this happens in a day).
